diagnosis.text: I have a calc exam friday and I genuinely don't think I'm smart enough to pass, I don't even know where to start
diagnosis.insight: You're treating the whole exam as one undefined wall instead of a sequence of small problems; 'not smart enough' is the wall talking, not your actual ability.
diagnosis.tip: Pick one single calc problem and do just the first step.

diagnosis.text: my capstone report is like 40 pages and it's so huge I just freeze every time I open it
diagnosis.insight: Freezing when you open the file means the next step isn't defined yet—your brain sees a mountain, not a path.
diagnosis.tip: Open a blank doc and list three tiny next steps.

diagnosis.text: the coding assignment uses recursion and I don't get it at all, I keep rereading the prompt
diagnosis.insight: Rereading the same prompt over and over usually means the concept itself feels like a wall, not that you're missing one detail.
diagnosis.tip: Draw one tiny recursion example on paper.

diagnosis.text: i'm stuck on my essay, i don't know what to write next and i feel like it'll be bad anyway
diagnosis.insight: Not knowing the next line usually means the step isn't small enough yet, not that you're out of ideas.
diagnosis.tip: Write the next sentence, even if it's messy.

diagnosis.text: why do I even need to take this gen ed history class, the reading is so boring and has nothing to do with my major
diagnosis.insight: You called the reading boring and irrelevant to your major, so the payoff feels near zero right now.
diagnosis.tip: Find one link between this class and your major

diagnosis.text: this worksheet is pointless busywork, I don't care about it at all
diagnosis.insight: Calling it 'pointless busywork' means the reward feels invisible, not that the work itself is necessarily meaningless.
diagnosis.tip: Pick one real-life reason this matters to you.

diagnosis.text: I have to write a reflection journal and it feels so useless, who even reads these
diagnosis.insight: Asking 'who even reads these' shows the block isn't writing skill—it's that the journal feels like homework for an invisible audience instead of something useful to you.
diagnosis.tip: Write one sentence about what actually happened today.

diagnosis.text: the lab writeup is so tedious and boring, I'd rather do literally anything else
diagnosis.insight: The writeup offers no immediate payoff, so your brain treats it as a cost with zero reward.
diagnosis.tip: Pair the writeup with a favorite snack or playlist.

diagnosis.text: every time I sit down to study I end up on tiktok for an hour
diagnosis.insight: The moment you sit down, your phone offers an instant reward that outcompetes studying before you even begin.
diagnosis.tip: Put your phone in another room before you start.

diagnosis.text: I keep checking my phone and discord, I can't stay on my problem set for more than 2 minutes
diagnosis.insight: Two minutes is the phone's reward speed; Discord pays off instantly while the problem set pays off much later.
diagnosis.tip: Put your phone in another room for 10 minutes.

diagnosis.text: I started reading but then I started cleaning my room and then youtube and now it's midnight
diagnosis.insight: Your attention jumped from reading to cleaning to YouTube, each offering a faster reward than the task.
diagnosis.tip: Put your phone in another room for 10 minutes.

diagnosis.text: my roommate is gaming next to me and I keep getting distracted and joining in
diagnosis.insight: Gaming with your roommate pays off in seconds, while studying pays off later, so your brain picks the immediate win.
diagnosis.tip: Put on headphones and move to a different room.

diagnosis.text: the research paper isn't due for three weeks so I haven't started, there's plenty of time
diagnosis.insight: A three-week gap makes the deadline feel abstract, so your brain files it as 'later' instead of 'now'.
diagnosis.tip: Set a fake deadline for this Friday.

diagnosis.text: the final is in december, that feels so far away I can't make myself care yet
diagnosis.insight: A December final feels abstract now, so your brain treats the payoff as too distant to motivate action today.
diagnosis.tip: Set a fake deadline for next Friday instead of December.

diagnosis.text: I always wait until the night before because the deadline doesn't feel real until then, it's due next month
diagnosis.insight: Your deadline is weeks away, so your brain files it under 'someday' instead of 'now'—that's why it only feels real the night before.
diagnosis.tip: Set a fake deadline for this Friday instead.

diagnosis.text: project's due in like 2 weeks, I'll start next weekend probably
diagnosis.insight: Two weeks feels like forever, so your brain treats 'next weekend' as real and the deadline as fiction.
diagnosis.tip: Set a fake deadline for this Friday instead.
